skill.name: generate-output
skill.description: Create complete code, documentation, tests, or content from validated requirements while following saved project standards.
skill.summary: Generate ready-to-use deliverables that match project standards and user requirements.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

security_audit.summary: All five static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. The command-execution findings are Markdown fences or inline path formatting, and no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or system reconnaissance behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - If unsure about a detail, follow their anti-patterns guidance (do opposite of what they said to av

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 81-91 contain a fenced JavaScript example that calls standardsRepository.getStandards. There is no shell execution or Ruby backtick use.
Line 91 is only the closing fence of a Markdown code block. It does not execute a command or describe command execution.
Line 93 uses inline Markdown backticks around a local documentation path. It is a reference to documentation, not shell execution.
Line 99 opens a Markdown output-format fence. The block is a template for deliverable structure, not executable shell or Ruby code.
Line 150 tells the assistant to avoid user-defined anti-patterns. It contains no system reconnaissance command or request to inspect host information.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time turning validated requirements into consistent deliverables. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create complete outputs that follow project standards.
actual_capabilities: Generates code, documentation, tests, refactors, or content from validated requirements.
Applies saved project principles and common patterns when standards are available.
Uses a consistent output format with summary, applied principles, deliverable, and next steps.
Adds supporting elements such as examples, comments, error handling, or tests when relevant.
Adapts guidance for code features, documentation, refactoring, test suites, and content creation.
limitations: Requires clear validated requirements from an earlier workflow step.
Depends on available project standards for exact style and pattern matching.
Does not run generated code or tests by itself.
May need human review for domain rules, security requirements, or production release decisions.

use_cases.title: Build a Feature From Approved Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn a validated feature request into complete code with supporting examples and implementation notes.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Generate structured documentation that follows the project template, tone, and example style.

use_cases.title: Produce Test Coverage Plans
use_cases.description: Create maintainable test suites that cover normal behavior, edge cases, setup, and teardown.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Deliverable
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-output to create the requested deliverable from these validated requirements: [paste requirements]. Include a short summary and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-output for this project type: [project type]. Follow these standards: [paste principles and patterns]. Produce a complete ready-to-use output.

prompt_templates.title: Create Code With Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-output to implement this feature: [feature]. Include production code, error handling, example usage, and tests for key edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor and Explain Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-output to refactor this validated target: [paste context]. Show the improved result, explain changes, and note behavioral differences.

output_examples.input: Validated requirement for a searchable dropdown component with keyboard navigation.
output_examples.output: A complete component plan with typed properties, keyboard behavior, error handling, usage notes, and test coverage recommendations.

output_examples.input: Validated request for onboarding documentation for a new internal tool.
output_examples.output: A structured guide with overview, setup steps, examples, troubleshooting notes, related links, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Validated request to improve a brittle test suite.
output_examples.output: A revised test suite outline covering normal behavior, edge cases, setup, teardown, and naming conventions.

best_practices: Provide validated requirements before using the skill.
Include project type, audience, standards, and required output format.
Review generated deliverables before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague requests without acceptance criteria.
Do not skip project standards when they exist.
Do not treat generated output as tested or released without verification.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates code, documentation, tests, refactors, and written content from validated requirements.

faq.question: Does it require a standards file?
faq.answer: No. It can use best practices when standards are unavailable, but standards improve consistency.

faq.question: Can it run tests after generation?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes and creates deliverables, but execution requires the host assistant or user.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this only for software projects?
faq.answer: No. It also supports documentation, test planning, refactoring, and general content creation.

faq.question: How should users prepare inputs?
faq.answer: Provide approved requirements, project type, relevant standards, target audience, and any required constraints.
